messages:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> service=redwood-edge, incident=INC-2026-045, symptom=TLS handshake failures (client TLS error) in eu-west-1. Trigger: 502 rate > 3% over 5m. Paging primary oncall @maria and escalation path set.

ops-bot: created thread and pinned initial alert, collecting logs and metrics. Notifying network and infra.

maria: acked. I'm on it. grabbing quick metrics, please post any relevant lb/target logs here.

samir: seeing repeated `tls: handshake failure` in edge-proxy logs for targets in eu-west-1. sample from edge-node-12: `2026-03-15T12:46:03Z error tls: handshake error from 10.0.2.45: remote error: tls: bad certificate`

jon: metrics from observability: 12:43 → 12:56 spike in 502/503s for eu-west-1. user impact ~7.2% of successful requests turned 502, p95 latency up ~180ms. request volume unchanged. US regions normal.

tess: FYI we rolled cert-rotator job at 12:37 — it pushed new certs to edge pool A as part of the quarterly rotation canary. job logs show a few transient failures but reported success overall.

maria: hypothesis: bad cert rollout to edge pool A causing ALB target group health to fail and TLS handshakes to break. plan: fail traffic off pool A to pool B, revert certs on a small subset if needed, and monitor. Samir, can you confirm target health? Jon, prepare rollback telemetry.

samir: checking ALB target groups now. `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:...:tg/eu-west-1/edge-pool-a` -> many targets marked unhealthy with reason `tlsHandshakeError`/`target-response-timeout`.

jon: pushing a quick traffic shift: updating weighted routing to route 100% to pool-B in eu-west-1. command: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://weight-change.json` (running now).

ops-bot: pagerduty-bot: incident acknowledged by maria (primary oncall). Auto-escalation paused.

alan: executed traffic shift, confirmed via curl from eu probe: before -> `curl -v https://edge.redwood.example.com` showed `* SSL: certificate subject name does not match` then `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway`. After weight switch -> `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`.

samir: target health for pool-A still unhealthy. pool-B targets all healthy. ALB metrics show surge in unhealthy hosts falling from 40->3 in last 3 minutes after weight shift.

maria: good. hold for 5 more minutes, then slowly bring pool-A back with new certs or rollback. Could be cert chain or mis-signed key in rotator. Tess, can you fetch the cert details that rotator deployed?

tess: pulling cert metadata: rotator pushed cert serial 0x9f3a at 12:37. Thumbprint doesn't match what the canary validator expected earlier (validator reported mismatch for 2 hosts but ignored error). I'm rolling back rotator on shard subset now.

jon: quick check on DNS: we recently lowered RR TTL to 60s for rollout window, so weight flip should propagate quickly. still seeing a few probe failures from legacy ISPs (they might cache).

samir: initiating selective rollback on 4 problematic nodes and restarting edge-proxy there. restart logs: `rotator: restore cert serial 0x8b2d` applied, edge-proxy comes up and passes TLS verify.

alan: after rollback and restarts, I see target health for those 4 nodes recover. running additional health checks.

maria: customer impact summary so far: window ~12:43–12:56, region eu-west-1, roughly 7% of foreground API calls got 5xx. Affected customers: mostly EU-based app endpoints; no data corruption, just increased error rates. Incident severity: page (S2 -> S1 if prolonged).

jon: adding a dashboard link: https://observability.redwood/example/charts/edge-eu-tls (link to internal graph). p95 latency back to baseline, error rate trending down to <0.3% now.

ops-bot: pagerduty-bot: reminder — escalation windows will resume if error > 2% for >10m. Currently under threshold.

tess: rotator job fixed to actually fail the pipeline if validator mismatch happens (it previously logged and continued). I've opened PR to change behavior and will add a canary check step.

maria: handoff: I'm going to end active mitigation and hand to oncall follow-up for postmortem and RCA. Assigning to samir for primary follow-up and tess for infra/process changes.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged and resolved by maria. Incident status -> resolved. Duration ~27m.

maria: postmortem notes to include: (1) make cert validator strict, (2) add pre-rotation canary checks that verify TLS handshake end-to-end, (3) add alert that cert-rotator reported validator mismatch as an active pager. Also follow-up: confirm we have rollback playbook for rotations (I've linked runbook edit PR in #eng-runbooks).

samir: will own the postmortem doc. capturing timeline and logs. tagging impacted customer list for outreach.

alan: thumbs up. added incident tag to oncall board and created follow-up tickets for monitoring and runbook updates.

maria: closing thread — monitoring for 30m then will file final report. great rapid response everyone :thumbsup:

ops-bot: thread archived (auto) and summary saved to incidents/3332101234 for postmortem reference.
